title: Lift a full 3 kg soup pot by both handles and pour the soup into a tureen
instruction: Lift the full pot of soup (about 3 kg) off the hob by both handles, pour all of the soup into the white tureen without spilling, and set the pot back down on the hob.
context: The skill is two arms lifting, carrying and tipping one heavy two-handled pot together and setting it back down, as when serving soup from a full pot at home or in a restaurant kitchen. This 3 L pot weighs 3.0 kg with its 1.8 kg of soup: held by one handle it swings down about that handle, so both arms must lift, tip and lower it as one, steadily enough that nothing spills.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A portable single hob, fixed to the table: a dark body 20 cm square and 4.5 cm tall with a black glass top, a grey burner ring 17.6 cm across and a control knob on its front, its centre 18 cm forward on the centre line. (2) A stainless steel pot with straight sides and a rolled rim, inside 18 cm across and 12 cm deep (3 L; walls 4 mm), 1.2 kg empty, loose, standing centred on the hob. It has two cast-steel loop handles lying flat and sticking straight out to the left and to the right (toward the two arms): each is a horizontal U of 16 mm round steel whose two posts are 6.4 cm apart (centres) and whose outer bar, running front to back, stands 3.5 cm out from the wall (outer face), leaving a 1.9 cm gap inside; the handles are 10 cm above the pot's underside. (3) The soup: 1.8 kg, as 120 orange plastic beads 24 mm across, 15 g each (1.8 L of soup weighs about 1.8 kg), filling the pot about 7 cm deep. The full pot weighs 3.0 kg. (4) A white soup tureen, inside 20 cm across and 8.7 cm deep (2.7 L), its rim 9.5 cm above the table, fixed to the table with its centre 40 cm forward on the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Counted at the end of the trial, placing each bead by its centre. 0.0 if at any time the pot tilts 30 degrees or more while the lowest point of its body (base or rim) is within 6 cm of the table (tipped over on the hob rather than lifted), or if it ends tilted 30 degrees or more. Otherwise 1.0 with at least 102 of the 120 beads in the tureen, at most 5 spilled (outside both the pot and the tureen) and the pot back upright on the hob (tilted less than 10 degrees, its centre within 3 cm of the hob's centre and its underside within 1 cm of the hob's top); 0.5 with at least 60 beads in the tureen and at most 12 spilled; 0.25 with at least 12 in the tureen; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: tip the beads from the tureen back into the pot and stand the pot back on the hob with its handles pointing left and right.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table; robot gains and gripper force (50 N) unchanged. The soup is a rigid-bead stand-in: 120 rigid 24 mm beads of 15 g, 1.8 kg in all (the weight of 1.8 L of soup), that pour and roll but do not slosh, splash or flow like liquid. Round walls are 32 flat segments; the hob and tureen are fixed. The full pot (3.0 kg, 1.5 kg per arm) is within the YAM's ~2 kg per-arm payload.
